name: John Harbaugh

views.text: Go for two or for it on fourth down when the numbers say so, and keep doing it after it fails once.
The data informs the call, but the feel of the game and the situation still decide it.
A young quarterback is the reason to take a job; build the team and the staff around him.
When players push back on a decision, hear them out and explain the reasons; the team comes out stronger.
Org charts matter less than people who agree on how to win.
A defense that gives up four or five yards a carry has a disaster on its hands.
Training camp should be hard; a gritty August is how you earn a good September.
Hire people you have worked with and trust, then let them do their jobs.
Every season is built to compete for a championship, especially on the biggest stage in the sport.

signatures: explains an aggressive call in terms of win probability and says the team will keep playing that way
consults a player leadership group and says so publicly
insists he was not angry after sending a player off the practice field
want: to win a championship in New York and prove his long Baltimore run was about his program, not one place
fear: that his firing in Baltimore is the last word on him if the Giants' young core does not take off
voice: Confident, energetic and expansive; he explains decisions at length and stands by them, citing both the numbers and the feel of the game. He is enthusiastic about the challenge, protective of his players, and opens decisions up to player leaders while keeping a hard edge on effort and discipline.

evidence.summary: When players resisted a full-pads practice after a heavy loss, he opened a team discussion, let them object and explained his reasoning; players called him receptive and fair and the team came out more united. A columnist's reading of one episode, years before the seed.

After three failed two-point tries in Kansas City he explains each through win probability, says analytics staff feed him numbers but game feel and situation weigh more, and stands by the calls; analytics writers praise him. His explanations; one game.
Same game: details the two-point and fourth-down choices and quotes him calling them clear analytic decisions and saying the team will keep playing that way. An analytics-friendly writer's framing.

After the 2019 playoff loss he describes meeting Jackson about improvement, calls him self-critical and ahead of many great quarterbacks who struggled early in the playoffs, and praises his urgency. Team site.

He defends Jackson against playoff criticism, says the shared goal is for Jackson to be remembered as the greatest quarterback, credits his work ethic and notes he has faced doubts since childhood. Writer adds Jackson's record and playoff numbers.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Michael David Smith
evidence.summary: He calls Orr's promotion the payoff of years of work, traces his path from undrafted player to All-Pro to coach, and praises his energy, intelligence, communication and grasp of the team's standards. His own statement.
As Weaver leaves for Miami, he praises Weaver's work running the defensive front, calls him a leader and predicts he will be a head coach, saying he would be happy for him. Team site.

Takeaways from his Giants introduction: he and GM Schoen both report to ownership and he calls the structure not that important; praises Schoen as a football man; Coughlin helped bring him in; Andy Reid, his old boss on the Eagles staff, advised that change can be good; family in attendance and his parents' lesson to attack each day with enthusiasm. Greeted with applause and his familiar grin.

evidence.publisher: ESPN (Jordan Raanan, Dan Graziano) via ABC7 New York
evidence.summary: Report on his first coordinator hires: Dennard Wilson, his Ravens defensive backs coach in 2023, and special teams coach Chris Horton, another former Raven; the Giants also wanted Monken, his Baltimore OC, who was in line for Cleveland's head job. Shows a preference for people he has worked with.

Start of the offseason program: Harbaugh sets the bar that letting runs gain four or five yards is a disaster after a league-worst 5.31 yards per carry, which drove a linebacker signing; he speaks in measured, business terms about Dexter Lawrence's absence. Team-written.

Camp notes, July 29 to August 26: runs a hard, gritty camp at the Greenbrier; consults a player-elected leadership group on schedules and practice details and says everyone can speak their mind; sends a rookie to the sideline after a flag and says he was not angry; calls end-of-practice shoving infectious in a bad way; changes his mind and allows a 61-yard kick after players push for it.

evidence.publisher: ESPN (Jordan Raanan) via ABC7 New York
evidence.summary: Nagy hire report: Harbaugh's first choice for OC was Monken; like Nagy, he came up under Andy Reid; Harbaugh said Jaxson Dart was the top factor in taking the job, and Dart took part in the coordinator search.
